primary_responsibility: Manages the lifecycle of user subscriptions, including creation, cancellation, renewal, and integration with external payment providers.

functional_group_candidates.name: Subscription Lifecycle Management
functional_group_candidates.user_goal: Manage the full lifecycle of a SaaS subscription from creation to cancellation
business_rules: User cannot have more than one active subscription
Subscription plan must be available to be selected
Paid plans require successful Stripe subscription creation before activation
Billing dates are calculated based on plan interval (monthly, yearly, weekly)
Features are granted upon activation and revoked upon immediate cancellation
Failed payments transition subscription status to past_due

functional_group_candidates.name: Billing and Payment Processing
functional_group_candidates.user_goal: Process payments and handle billing cycles for paid subscriptions
business_rules: Renewal requires successful payment for paid plans
Usage records must be created upon successful billing/renewal
Next billing date must be updated upon successful renewal
Users must be notified of confirmations, renewals, and payment failures

quality_issues.title: Network Call Inside Database Transaction
quality_issues.evidence: ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do ... stripe_subscription = create_stripe_subscription(user, plan, payment_method_id) ... end (lines 24-49)
quality_issues.why_it_matters: Holding a database transaction open while waiting for an external API (Stripe) can lead to connection pool exhaustion and database locking. This significantly impacts application scalability and reliability, as the DB connection is tied up for the duration of the network round-trip.
quality_issues.suggested_fix: Perform the Stripe API call before opening the ActiveRecord transaction. Use the transaction only for local database updates and handle rollbacks manually or via state management if the API call succeeded but the DB update failed.

quality_issues.title: Generic Rescue of StandardError
quality_issues.why_it_matters: Rescuing StandardError catches all exceptions, including syntax errors, NameErrors, and NoMethodErrors. This masks bugs and makes debugging difficult. It also returns a generic error message to the caller which might contain sensitive system details via e.message.
quality_issues.suggested_fix: Rescue specific exceptions (e.g., Stripe::StripeError, ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) and let unexpected system errors bubble up to global error handlers.

quality_issues.title: N+1 Query in Feature Management
quality_issues.why_it_matters: The code executes a separate database query for every feature in the plan. If a plan has many features, this results in significant overhead and latency due to multiple round-trips to the database.
quality_issues.suggested_fix: Use a single query to fetch existing feature access records for the user and perform a bulk insert or use `upsert_all` for the new features.

quality_issues.title: Inconsistent Transactional Integrity in Renewal
quality_issues.why_it_matters: Unlike the creation and cancellation methods, the renewal process is not wrapped in a transaction. If `create_subscription_usage_record` fails, the subscription will have been updated with a new billing date, but no usage record will exist, leading to data inconsistency.
quality_issues.suggested_fix: Wrap the updates in `process_renewal` within an `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction` block.

quality_issues.title: Potential Race Condition in Subscription Check
quality_issues.evidence: return error_result('User already has active subscription') if user.subscription&.active? (line 17)
quality_issues.why_it_matters: The check for an existing subscription happens before the transaction starts. Two concurrent requests for the same user could pass this check simultaneously, leading to duplicate active subscriptions.
quality_issues.suggested_fix: Add a unique database index on user_id for active subscriptions or use a row-level lock (e.g., `user.lock!`) inside the transaction.

opportunities: Move billing interval logic (lines 115-123) into the `SubscriptionPlan` model or a dedicated Value Object to improve encapsulation.
Offload notification sending (lines 43, 83, 108) to background jobs (ActiveJob) to reduce latency in the main request/response cycle.
Consider using a state machine (e.g., AASM) to manage subscription status transitions (pending -> active -> cancelled) to ensure valid state flows.
Extract feature granting/revocation logic into a separate domain service or concern to reduce the size and complexity of SubscriptionService.
Use Rails' built-in 'Enums' for subscription status to improve queryability and provide helper methods.
